LESSON: MAP READING AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Map Reading and Interpretation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Map Reading and Interpretation, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. interpret maps using marginal information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Map Reading and Interpretation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. calculate areas of places on a topographical map,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Map Reading and Interpretation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the different methods of representing physical features on topographical maps,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Map Reading and Interpretation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply critical thinking skills in map interpretation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Map Reading and Interpretation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. value map reading and interpretation in day- to - day life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Map Reading and Interpretation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. interpret maps using marginal information,

   Map Reading and Interpretation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. describe the different methods of representing physical features on topographical maps,

   Map Reading and Interpretation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. apply critical thinking skills in map interpretation,

E. value map reading and interpretation in day- to - day life.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. exchange new ideas

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Map Reading and Interpretation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: Learners exchange new ideas when discussing in groups the marginal information on a map.

● Digital Literacy: Learners use digital devices to search for essential critical thinking skills necessary for map

interpretation.

Values:
● Unity: Learners collaborate with others when practicing scale conversions on a topographical map.

● Responsibility: Learners accomplish the task of carrying out a research on different methods of representing physical

features.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: Learners work harmoniously in groups to practice scale conversions on a topographical map.

Link to other subjects:

● The learner applies drawing skills from Creative Arts in drawing diagrams of the relief and drainage features on a

topographical map.

● The learner applies calculation skills from Mathematics in working out the area of different places on a topographical map.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. interpret maps using marginal information,
2. calculate areas of places on a topographical map,
3. describe the different methods of representing physical features on topographical maps,
4. apply critical thinking skills in map interpretation,
5. value map reading and interpretation in day- to - day life.

Remember the key question: How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?
